clue.text: Look out — sprinkler ahead, he warns

indicators.note: ahead tells us the golfer's warning goes in front of the sprinkler

parts.note: Fore! is the golfer's shout warning people in the path of a struck ball
a caster (or castor) is a pot with a perforated lid for sprinkling sugar or salt

explanation.surface: A warning shout as someone with a garden sprinkler approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look out' reads as part of the warning but is the golfer's shout; 'ahead' sets it before the sugar sprinkler.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecaster's job is predicting storms and alerting the public to them.

clue.text: Eager to simulate sound

indicators.note: sound says the word for simulate is to be taken as heard aloud

parts.note: to feign is to simulate, pretend

explanation.walkthrough: FEIGN (simulate) sounds like the answer; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for glad or willing, as in 'I would fain go'.

clue.text: Train attendants

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about railway staff; each word defines the answer alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a train, the body of followers behind a great person, and those followers are the great person's attendants.

clue.text: Lounge lizard is on the floor by evening, we hear

parts.note: a carpet lies on the floor

indicators.note: we hear says the word for evening is spoken, giving a title-holder

parts.note: night is the evening

explanation.surface: A drunken idler is lying on the floor by nightfall, so rumour says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'by' are links: CARPET then KNIGHT, sounding like NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet knight is a soldier who idles at home in drawing rooms rather than fighting, a ladies' man.

clue.text: Furtive about re-writing novel in a dirty way

indicators.note: about says the furtive word is placed around the other letters

parts.note: sly means furtive, secretive

indicators.note: re-writing says the letters of novel are put down in a new order

explanation.surface: A secretive author reworks a novel in a smutty fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-writing' shuffles the novel's letters, and 'about' wraps the furtive word around them; 'dirty' reads as smutty but means unkempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenly means untidy and careless, unwashed in appearance or habits.

clue.text: Useful preparation for a good upbringing

definitions.text: Useful preparation for a good upbringing

parts.words: Useful preparation for a good upbringing
parts.note: a medicinal preparation that makes a patient vomit, bringing up the stomach's contents

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upbringing' suggests child rearing, but it means bringing up food.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug given to induce vomiting, used to clear poison from the stomach.

clue.text: This is short notice for a departure

definitions.text: This is short notice for a departure

parts.words: This is short notice for a departure
parts.note: a departure here is a death, and the notice of it in a newspaper is given in a shortened form of its name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short notice' sounds like little warning, but it means a clipped word for a death notice; 'departure' is a euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an abbreviation of obituary, a newspaper notice reporting someone's death.

clue.text: A redcap, perhaps, protecting an eminence

definitions.text: A redcap, perhaps, protecting an eminence

parts.words: A redcap, perhaps, protecting an eminence
parts.note: the square red hat worn by a cardinal, who is addressed as Your Eminence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Redcap' suggests a military policeman and 'eminence' a hill; it is a cardinal's red cap, and a cardinal is styled His Eminence.
explanation.definitionFit: The biretta is the stiff square cap of Catholic clergy, scarlet for cardinals.

clue.text: By craft informer is in a position to accept money

indicators.note: by means next to, so the informer is set beside the craft

parts.note: a teller is one who tells, an informer
a ship is a craft

explanation.surface: Through cunning, a grass is well placed to take bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' reads as cunning but is a SHIP; 'is in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank teller's post involves receiving and paying out cash over the counter.

clue.text: Banded together to veto winner somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the two words are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: A coalition forms to block a victor's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges VETO and WINNER; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads woven in and out of each other form bands joined into one fabric.

clue.text: Vocal during corporal punishment

indicators.note: during says the answer runs inside the words that follow, within their letters

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out while a caning is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' points to the letters sitting inside 'corporal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something spoken by mouth rather than written.

clue.text: One appears in a drag masque dancing on the Sabbath

indicators.note: dancing says the letters of a drag masque, with one added, move into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone turns up at a drag ball held on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' adds I (one) to A DRAG MASQUE, and 'dancing' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadragesima is the first Sunday in Lent, forty days before Easter.

clue.text: Kind of bender the vanquished go on

definitions.text: Kind of bender the vanquished go on

parts.words: Kind of bender the vanquished go on
parts.note: a joint that bends, and the part of the leg the defeated sink down onto in submission

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' suggests a drinking spree, but it is simply something that bends, the leg joint people sink onto when beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint flexes, and the beaten are said to be brought down onto it in surrender.

clue.text: Code of conduct, for strikers of course

definitions.text: Code of conduct, for strikers of course

parts.words: Code of conduct, for strikers of course
parts.note: a set of manners, which those who strike a ball with a cue are naturally expected to follow, as the word's middle sounds like cue

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests a union picket, but here it means billiard players, who strike with a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the accepted set of polite rules for behaviour in a group or setting.

clue.text: They are invited to stay in the country, to arrange her autopsy

definitions.text: They are invited to stay in the country

indicators.note: to arrange is to set the letters of her autopsy out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Country-house guests are called on to set up a post-mortem, as in a detective story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' shuffles HER AUTOPSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of guests staying several days at a country home.

clue.text: More capacity than is needed for deliveries by butcher

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler
to butcher is to slaughter, to kill

explanation.surface: A butcher's van brings far more meat than the shop can hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' looks like van rounds but is cricket's set of six balls bowled; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess destructive force, beyond what the job requires, is the original military sense.

clue.text: People susceptible to publicity for a dead body

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
a mass is a body of matter or of people

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; A plus D (dead) plus MASS (body) builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the mass public whom advertisers target, seen as easily swayed by commercials.

clue.text: Rely on possibly Swiss funds

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a Swiss roll is a rolled sponge cake, so a roll may be Swiss

explanation.surface: Count on a Swiss account for your money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss' suggests banking, but a Swiss roll is a rolled sponge cake, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bankroll is a supply of money, a wad of notes or the capital behind a venture.

clue.text: Impassive girl much taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback says the girl and much together are read backwards

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, for Diana
lots means much, a great deal

explanation.surface: A girl remains unmoved though greatly startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like the girl's state of shock, but it signals the girl and 'much' read backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person shows little emotion and is hard to excite.

clue.text: Order learner to ski somehow to the reference mark

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of ski are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A beginner is told to ski over to the marker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns SKI into ISK; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the obelisk is the dagger sign (†) used to point to a footnote.

clue.text: It's the East End for bad soldiers

definitions.text: It's the East End for bad soldiers

parts.words: It's the East End for bad soldiers
parts.note: the Eastern end, death, for disgraced Japanese warriors who took their own lives

explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' suggests London's East End, but it means an end, a death, in the East: Japanese ritual suicide by disgraced samurai.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual suicide by disembowelment was the traditional fate of Japanese samurai who had brought dishonour on themselves.

clue.text: Like the blinking sitter portrayed in the Mer, of Venice

definitions.text: Like the blinking sitter portrayed in the Mer, of Venice

parts.words: Like the blinking sitter portrayed in the Mer, of Venice
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice the Prince of Arragon opens the silver casket and finds the portrait of a blinking fool

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play the silver casket holds 'the portrait of a blinking idiot'; 'sitter' means the subject of that portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means foolish, like the fool in the portrait.

clue.text: "Shut up" freely translated into Persian

indicators.note: freely translated says the letters of shut up are rendered loosely in a new order

explanation.surface: A rude order rendered loosely in Farsi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely translated' rearranges SHUT UP; 'into' is a link. The answer is the Afghan language, of the Iranian family, so loosely Persian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pashto language belongs to the Iranian branch of languages, the family that includes Farsi.

clue.text: Kind of garment you don't expect to find reduced

definitions.text: Kind of garment you don't expect to find reduced

parts.words: Kind of garment you don't expect to find reduced
parts.note: clothing treated before sale so that it will not get smaller in the wash

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' suggests a sale price; it means shrunk, which a pre-treated garment will not be.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric shrunk in manufacture will not lose size when laundered.

clue.text: Classical departure for an actor

parts.note: the Latin word for he goes out, used as a stage direction telling a player to leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' means Latin: the stage direction is the Latin for 'he goes out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction tells a player to leave the stage.

clue.text: Mark Sheridan made a trip to this borough

definitions.text: Sheridan made a trip to this borough

explanation.surface: The music-hall star Mark Sheridan visited a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Sheridan was a music-hall comedian, but here 'Mark' is the definition; R B Sheridan wrote the play A Trip to Scarborough, and this word plus 'borough' gives that Yorkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left by a healed wound, and with 'borough' added it names the town in Sheridan's play title.

clue.text: Sadie Thompson's downfall

parts.note: the title of Somerset Maugham's story about the prostitute Sadie Thompson, and a literal falling of water

explanation.walkthrough: Sadie Thompson is the heroine of Somerset Maugham's story of that title, set during a monsoon; 'downfall' is both her ruin and a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is literally water falling, and Maugham named his Sadie Thompson story after the weather.

clue.text: Made from log chips, it used to be combustible

indicators.note: made from says the answer is put together out of the reshuffled letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A fire-lighter made out of wood chippings once burnt well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made from' rearranges LOG CHIPS IT. 'Used to be' marks the definition as obsolete science.
explanation.definitionFit: The discarded theory of phlogiston held that burnable things contained a fire-element released on burning.

clue.text: Satisfactory in the old-fashioned collar

indicators.note: in says satisfactory sits inside the old form of the

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
OK means satisfactory, all right

explanation.surface: An antique collar is passed as acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' signals the archaic spelling seen on signs like 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden yoke is the frame fitted over an ox's neck, and a dress yoke is its fitted shoulder section.

clue.text: Luxury saloon for a chap with influence

definitions.text: Luxury saloon for a chap with influence

parts.words: Luxury saloon for a chap with influence
parts.note: a plush railway carriage, read as a vehicle for a man with pull, since pull means influence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a car or bar; it is a luxurious railway carriage named after George Pullman, readable as a car for a man with pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pullman built lavishly fitted railway carriages, and his name became the word for them.
